title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 30.00 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2020 Land Area 30.00 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is not an official government website. It is a community-run project that operates independently of the Local Government Unit. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent community project and is not an official website of the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

body: Independent · Citizen-Maintained · Pangasinan Mapandan, in the open. Officials, budgets, ordinances, and frontline services for the Municipality of Mapandan — gathered from public records and kept in one place, so every resident can find what their local government is doing. Browse Services See the Budget Find a Service Search every service Mapandan offers — by what you're trying to do, not which office handles it. Popular: business permit local hospital barangay clearance tax declaration 38,228 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Residents 15 Official Source: DILG / Comelec Barangays 9,326 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Households 1,274/km² Official Computed: 38,228 ÷ 30.00 km² Pop. density 30.00 km² Official Source: MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Land area Third-Class Municipality · Region I A rice-growing town in Pangasinan's third district Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 30 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. A Brief History The Story of Mapandan From a new pueblo to a growing community Before 1887 Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed, the area belonged to Mangaldan as southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, and Amanoaoac. Read the founding story Ten local leaders — Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin — led the petition for a separate town. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background Dec. 28, 1887 Mapandan becomes a pueblo Established as an independent pueblo through Director General No. 39, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. Read more The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan. Its administrative seat was first set up in Barrio Torres, then relocated to present-day Poblacion on land donated by the Aquino family. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1887–1890s The first town center The first seat was in Barrio Torres, near a church where Fr. Jose Torres served. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants. Read more The Torres location proved inconvenient — too close to the southern boundary. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had been a sitio of Apaya. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Torres History; Barangay Poblacion History 1903 The epidemic A severe epidemic devastated the municipality, causing population loss, migration, and fiscal insolvency. The 1903 census recorded 4,198 residents. Read more The epidemic directly affected Mapandan’s ability to function as a municipality, leading to its temporary return to Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile; PSA Census 1903 1905–1908 Return to Mangaldan Due to financial insolvency, Mapandan temporarily surrendered its municipal status and was re-absorbed as part of Mangaldan. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1909 Mapandan rises again Re-established as an independent municipality under Executive Order No. 10, issued by Governor General James F. Smith. Read more After years of demographic and financial difficulties, Mapandan was reorganized and re-established as an independent municipality, beginning a new chapter of growth. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Municipal Profile — Historical Background 1940s War and reconstruction The Second World War interrupted development across Pangasinan. Postwar years brought land ownership changes and community rebuilding. Read more In the postwar years, tenants gained opportunities to own land they had been farming. Communities like Sta. Maria developed from hacienda land into independent barrios. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1965 Sta. Maria becomes a barrio Formerly a sitio of Luyan on hacienda land, Sta. Maria was established as a separate barrio, marking the growth of Mapandan’s community structure. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Sta. Maria History 1967 Golden becomes a barangay Formerly Amanoaoac North, Golden was established as a separate barangay. Named after the Golden Distillery that operated after liberation. Read more Golden underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, and cooperative organization. In 1972, it was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, with the award presented at Malacañang. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Golden History 1972–1973 Coral is established Created through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155, and Proclamation No. 11 (1973). Named after the stone coral enclosure built during the Spanish era. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Barangay Coral History 2002 Third-class municipality Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality, reflecting income and revenue growth under then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Physical Characteristics — Historical Development 2010s The Pandan Festival grows The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture, and community, held alongside the town fiesta. Source: Municipality of Mapandan, Official Website 2022–2024 Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the Mapandan Super Health Center. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, serving residents of all 15 barangays. Read more The 2022 General Appropriations Act included &₱circ;6.5 million for the facility. Phase 1 provides laboratory and dental services for Mapandan and nearby municipalities. Source: Philippine News Agency, March 15, 2024; DBM General Appropriations Act 2022 2024 Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228, continuing to invest in public services and community development. Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 POPCEN Mapandan Town Plaza Old Mapandan Public Market Early Municipal Officials Old Mapandan School Old Baloling Bridge ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Population through time Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) Stories Behind Our Barangays 15 communities, 15 histories Each of Mapandan’s barangays has its own story of origin, growth, and community life. Sources & Historical Notes Much of Mapandan’s historical material comes from the Municipality of Mapandan’s official website, including the Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, and individual barangay history pages. Population data is from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Development milestones reference the Philippine News Agency and Department of Budget and Management records. Some barangay histories attribute parts of their narratives to “old folks” / local oral histories. These are labeled as local historical accounts rather than independently documented facts. body: Sangguniang Bayan Legislative Documents A comprehensive database of municipal ordinances, resolutions, executive issuances, and fiscal data — tracing Mapandan's legislative record from its 1887 founding to the present. Framework Local governance & statutory origins Legal Basis The Municipality of Mapandan operates under Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), situated within the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan. The Sangguniang Bayan — a unicameral local legislative council — exercises municipal legislative power, presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor and composed of elected councilors alongside ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation. Historical Origins Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909. SB Ord. No. 7, S-2024 / SP Res. 1140-2024 Loan ₱28.5M Authorized CY 2020 Authorizes Mayor Anthony C. Peñuliar to utilize a remaining fund balance for extension of the public market, motorpool construction, and reinforced concrete wall. SB Ord. No. 1, S-2020 / SP Res. 1121-2020 Proposed Loan ₱45.0M Proposed CY 2026 Leverages LGU borrowing capacity to fund major municipal public works, infrastructure expansion, and LGU facility upgrades. SB Ord. No. 3, Series of 2026 View detailed fiscal data → Analysis Legislative trends Patterns in Mapandan's legislative output that reveal evolving public management strategies. Administrative Restructuring for Technical Capacity The Sangguniang Bayan has systematically eliminated redundant mid-level posts — such as the Agricultural Technologist (SG-10) under Ordinance No. 2, S-2021, the Assistant Municipal Treasury Head (SG-22) under Ordinance No. 1, S-2022, and the LDRRMO III (SG-18) under Ordinance No. 1, S-2026 — while creating specialized operational positions like Driver I (SG-3), Registration Officer I (SG-10), and elevating disaster management to department-head status via the MDRRM Officer position (SG-24). This strengthens disaster preparedness, civil registration, and frontline service delivery while optimizing payroll expenditures. National Mandate Devolution to Local Enforcement The municipal council translated national social policy into local enforcement: Ordinance No. 1, S-2025 institutionalizes the Mental Health Act (R.A. 11036), Ordinance No. 04, S-2025 establishes blood donation councils across all 15 barangays, Ordinance No. 6, S-2024 implements the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act (R.A. 9003) with local fees and penalties, and Ordinance No. 03, S-2025 extends benefits and incentives to Child Development Workers. National mandates are backed by dedicated local funding and village-level enforcement. Debt Financing for Capital Expansion Annual appropriations grew from ₱193.08M in CY 2025 to ₱218.21M in CY 2026 (a ~13% increase, SP Resolution No. 438-2026), largely committed to personal services and operations. Alongside this growth, the municipality has repeatedly turned to credit financing through state banks for capital projects: a ₱28.5M fund-utilization authorization in 2020 (Ordinance No. 1, S-2020) for market/motorpool works, a ₱28.8M Land Bank loan in 2024 (Ordinance No. 7, S-2024) for 16 rescue vehicles, and a ₱45M loan proposed in 2026 (Ordinance No. 3, S-2026) for infrastructure expansion — accelerating modernization while spreading obligations across future budget cycles. Land Use Planning and Reclassification Following the adoption of the Comprehensive Land Use Plan (SB Resolution No. 181, S-2023), the Sangguniang Bayan enacted the Integrated Zoning Regulations for 2022–2032 (Ordinance No. 4, S-2023) and passed successive land reclassification ordinances converting agricultural parcels to residential (Ordinance Nos. 2 and 3, S-2023, for subdivision development) and commercial use (Ordinance No. 5, S-2024), reflecting the municipality's shift toward planned urban and commercial expansion. Process Flow How an ordinance becomes law The legislative pipeline under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Provincial Review Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160. 9 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays. Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication. Database Architecture Strategic archival framework A structured schema for digital archival of legislative enactments, ensuring long-term data integrity and system interoperability. Field Name Data Type Definition Example Document_ID String (Primary Key) Unique system identifier: enactment type, year, and sequence ORD-2024-006 Issuing_Body Categorical Legislative or executive entity issuing the measure Sangguniang Bayan Document_Type Categorical Standard legal document classification Municipal Ordinance Document_Number String Official legislative designation and series number Ordinance No. 6, Series of 2024 Primary_Title Text Complete statutory title of the enactment An Ordinance Providing for Ecological Solid Waste Management... Date_Enacted_SB Date (ISO 8601) Date of final reading and passage by local council 2024-12-09 SP_Review_Resolution String Reviewing provincial board resolution reference Provincial Resolution No. 410-2025 SP_Review_Date Date (ISO 8601) Date of approval by Sangguniang Panlalawigan 2025-03-31 Fiscal_Value_PHP Decimal (12,2) Monetary value or loan amount authorized 28800000.00 Subject_Taxonomy Categorical Functional policy domain tagging Environment & Waste Management Verification_Status Categorical Whether the record was confirmed against the full source certification page or derived from title/URL only confirmed via SP certification Procedure 1 A dual-indexing mechanism links every municipal enactment ID directly to its corresponding Sangguniang Panlalawigan review resolution, preserving the complete chain of legal validity under the Local Government Code. Procedure 2 The digital repository organizes files using a categorical taxonomy: Fiscal & Budgetary Enactments; Personnel & Administrative Restructuring; Regulatory & Revenue Codes; Public Health, Safety, & Welfare; Land Use & Zoning; and Territorial & Boundary Decrees. Procedure 3 Physical archives at the Sangguniang Bayan Secretariat undergo OCR scanning into text-searchable PDF/A digital records, indexed alongside structured metadata for public legal research and ARTA compliance. Precedent Navarro v. Court of Appeals G.R. No. 141307, March 28, 2001 When Vice Mayor Baltazar Aquino assumed the mayoralty, the highest-ranking Sangguniang Bayan member elevated to Vice Mayor, opening a legislative seat. The Supreme Court ruled that the replacement had to come from the same political party as the vacating member, a precedent that continues to guide multi-tier local successions nationwide under Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code.

description: The Municipal Assessor's Office issues certified true copies of Tax Declarations for real properties located in Mapandan. This document shows the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements for taxation purposes.
body: Real Property & Revenue Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration Get a certified true copy of your Tax Declaration from the Assessor's Office. ₱100, 15 minutes processing. The Tax Declaration is an official document showing the assessed value of real property for taxation purposes. The client submits a written request with the property details. The Assessor's Office locates the record, prepares the certified true copy, and releases it upon payment. Requirements Written request stating the property location (lot number, block, street, barangay) Valid Government-issued ID Procedure Submit a written request with property details and valid ID to the Assessor's Office. Staff receives and verifies the request (5 min). Staff locates the Tax Declaration in the records (5 min). Staff prepares the certified true copy and stamps it (3 min). Pay ₱100 at the Treasury Office and claim the document (2 min). description: A birth certificate is a vital record issued by the Municipal Civil Registrar. body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Certificate Request a birth certificate from the Mapandan MCR. Standard ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. Description A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered birth certificates. This document is required for school enrollment, passport application, employment, and other legal purposes. Requirements Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party PSA copy of the birth certificate (if available, for verification) Barangay certification of residency (for the person named on the certificate) Affidavit of two disinterested persons (required for delayed registration only) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide the necessary supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified birth certificate upon release. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 10 minutes (standard) to 10+ days (late registration) Fee: ₱115 (standard) / ₱215 (unmarried) / ₱100 (hospital) / ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services No related services available.

title: Birth Registration — BetterMapandan.org
description: Registration of birth with the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers registration by attending midwife/hilot, unmarried parents, hospital administrators, and late registration with PSA verification.
body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth Registration Register a birth at the Mapandan MCR. Standard fee ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. Description Registration of birth at the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers three pathways: (1) Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth — requires Marriage Certificate of parents and Mun. Form 102; (2) Unmarried parents — requires Community Tax Certificate; (3) Hospital administrator — requires Accomplished Mun. Form 102. Late registration requires negative PSA certification and supporting documents. Fees: Misc Fee ₱115 (standard), ₱215 (unmarried), ₱100 (hospital), ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration depending on age). Requirements Marriage Certificate of parents from PSA (for attending midwife/hilot registration) Community Tax Certificate from Treasury Office (for unmarried parents) Accomplished Mun. Form 102 from MCR (for hospital registration) Negative certification from PSA (for late registration) Affidavit of delayed registration (for late registration) Supporting evidence: Baptismal Certificate, School records, ITR, Insurance Policy, Medical records, Barangay certification (for late registration) Procedure Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth. MCR evaluates information and registers (10 min). For unmarried parents: Hospital admin or representative prepares documents (15 min). For late registration: Apply at MCR, verify from CRIS/Registry Book. If negative, submit requirements. Data typed in Certificate of Live Birth (15 min typing). MCR approves registration (after 10 days of posting for late registration). Secure copy of birth certificate. MCR releases documents (3 min). title: Building Permit — BetterMapandan.org
description: A building permit is required under the National Building Code (PD 1096) and RA 11032. Processing times: Simple — 3 working days, Complex — 7 working days, Highly Technical — 20 working days. Includes site inspection, zoning and fire safety compliance.
body: Building, Engineering & Zoning Building Permit Get a building permit from the Mapandan MEO. Simple: 3 days, Complex: 7 days, Highly Technical: 20 days per RA 11032. Description A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Requirements Plans duly signed & sealed by licensed professionals Certified true copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor Office) Xerox copy of land title (from Register of Deeds) Community Tax Certificate (from Treasury Office) Latest Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Electrical & Sanitary permit (from Municipal Health Office) Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Certification from Barangay Captain Application for locational clearance (from Zoning Office) 2 Affidavits (from Notary Public) Affidavit of consent if not lot owner (from Notary Public) Fire Safety clearance (from BFP Office) Affidavit of adjoining lot owners Procedure Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Classification: Highly Technical Processing Time: 3 working days (Simple) / 7 working days (Complex) / 20 working days (Highly Technical) per RA 11032 Fee: Based on project cost (schedule per National Building Code) Where to Apply: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Building Appraisal / Assessment Occupancy Permit

title: New Business Permit — BetterMapandan.org
description: A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees.
body: Business Permitting & Licensing New Business Permit Apply for a new business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Includes endorsement to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP. Description A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: ~1 hour (10 min encoding + 44 min endorsement + 10 min pay & claim) Fee: Mayor's Permit (₱500–₱1,000) + Business Plate & Sticker (₱250) + Weights & Measure (₱100–200) + Storage Fee (₱550) + Garbage Fee (₱800–₱1,200) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Business Permit Renewal Business Zoning Clearance Mayor's Clearance & Certificates

title: Business Permit Renewal — BetterMapandan.org
description: Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing.
body: Business Permitting & Licensing Business Permit Renewal Renew your business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Annual renewal required to maintain compliance. Description Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP for required certificates (44 min). Pay fees at the Treasury Office. Fees include Mayor's Permit, Business Tax (% of Gross Sales), Plate & Sticker, Weights & Measure, Storage Fee, and Garbage Fee. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of renewed Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office. Service Details Responsible Office: Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: ~1 hour (similar to new business permit process) Fee: Mayor's Permit (₱500–₱1,000) + Business Tax (% of Gross Sales) + Business Plate & Sticker (₱250) + Weights & Measure (₱100–200) + Storage Fee (₱550) + Garbage Fee (₱800–₱1,200) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services New Business Permit Business Zoning Clearance

title: Business Zoning Clearance — BetterMapandan.org
description: A zoning clearance is required for all businesses applying for a business permit. The MPDC/Zoning Office encodes the business, conducts geotagging, computes fees, and issues the Business Zoning Clearance.
body: Zoning & Planning Business Zoning Clearance Get a business zoning clearance from the MPDC in Mapandan. Required before applying for a business permit. Description A zoning clearance is required for all businesses applying for a business permit. The MPDC/Zoning Office encodes the business to the DTI-Local Data Capture Sheet, conducts geotagging of the business establishment, computes fees in the iBPLS web application, and issues the Business Zoning Clearance. The process is part of the integrated business permit system. Requirements Unified Application Form for Business Permit (from BPLO) Procedure Go to MPDC / Zoning Office for zoning endorsement. MPDC encodes business to DTI-Local Data Capture Sheet Annex B. Geotagging of business establishment is conducted. Computation of fees in the iBPLS web application: Zoning fee (New Business ₱720, Renewal varies) + Inspection fee (₱100). MPDC prepares and issues Business Zoning Clearance. Complete endorsement is recorded. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Planning and Development Office (MPDC) / Zoning Office Classification: Simple Processing Time: ~24 minutes Fee: ₱820 (Zoning fee ₱720 + Inspection fee ₱100) Where to Apply: MPDC / Zoning Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services New Business Permit Business Permit Renewal Electrical Zoning Clearance

title: Cedula / Community Tax Certificate — BetterMapandan.org
description: The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) computation: Individual — ₱5.00 + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱5,000). Juridical — ₱500.00 + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱10,000). Interest of 24% per annum from March 1 to December 31.
body: Real Property & Revenue Cedula / Community Tax Certificate Get your Community Tax Certificate (cedula) in Mapandan. Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k; Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k. Description The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) is computed as follows: Individual — ₱5.00 basic + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income from business, profession, or property, but in no case shall exceed ₱5,000.00. Juridical — ₱500.00 basic + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income from business or worth of real property, but in no case shall exceed ₱10,000.00. Interest of 24% per annum shall be imposed on individual or juridical securing their CTC from March 1 up to the end of the year. Requirements Old Community Tax Certificate (if available) Proof of income (if available) Procedure Go to Counters 1 and 2 and fill up the basic data form (15 min). Pay the required fees (3 min). Receive community tax certificate. Staff records in general collection system (2 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 20 minutes (15 min form filling + 3 min payment + 2 min recording) Fee: Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k income (max ₱5,000); Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k income (max ₱10,000); 24% interest from March 1 Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services No related services available.

title: Certificate of Indigency — BetterMapandan.org
description: A Certificate of Indigency is issued to indigent families certified by the Barangay Captain. It is used to avail of hospital discounts, legal assistance from PAO, scholarship assistance, and other social services.
body: Social Welfare — IDs & Certifications Certificate of Indigency Get a Certificate of Indigency from the MSWDO for hospital discounts, legal aid, scholarships, and other social services. Description The Certificate of Indigency is issued by the MSWDO to indigent families certified by the Barangay Captain. Staff will refer you and conduct an initial interview. Submit your Barangay Certificate of Indigency and other supporting documents. Staff will conduct an interview and assess your eligibility for assistance. Receive your Certificate of Indigency upon approval. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 30 minutes Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services AICS Assistance Social Case Study Report LGU PhilHealth Group Enrollment

title: Children in Difficult Circumstances (CICL) — BetterMapandan.org
description: The MSWDO provides care and protection services for Children in Conflict with the Law (CICL) and children under difficult circumstances, including abandoned, neglected, physically and sexually abused, and emotionally abused children.
body: Social Assistance & Protection Children in Difficult Circumstances (CICL) MSWDO protection services for children in difficult circumstances in Mapandan. Counselling, shelter, and referral available. Description The MSWDO provides care and protection services for Children in Conflict with the Law (CICL) and children under difficult circumstances. Services include surveillance, rescue and recovery, counselling, referral to PNP, temporary shelter, and custody care. The MSWDO coordinates with the PNP, hospitals, and Prosecutor's Office as necessary. Requirements Birth Certificate (PSA) Medical Certificate / Medico-legal report Police Blotter Report Procedure Register at the MSWD Office. Staff will refer the client for intake. Discuss the problem and provide relevant information. Staff interviews and gathers data. Staff refers the client to other agencies (PNP, Hospital, Prosecutor's Office) if necessary. Staff prepares draft of Social Case Study Report and follows up with home visits and counseling. Present results. MSWDO prepares and submits Social Case Study Report. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 1 hour or more Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Women's Welfare (WSDW) Special Social Services

title: Birth / Marriage / Death Certifications — BetterMapandan.org

body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Birth / Marriage / Death Certifications Get certified copies of birth, marriage, or death certificates at the Mapandan MCR. ₱115 per copy. Present OR to MCR Office. Documents released. For PSA endorsement: MCR verifies and prepares endorsement (₱200, 10 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Processing Time: ~18 minutes Fee: ₱115 per copy; ₱200 for PSA endorsement Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar's Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Birth Certificate Death Certificate Marriage License

MCR examines documents and prepares amended COLB (20 min, ₱515). title: Crop Protection Technical Services — BetterMapandan.org

body: Agriculture Crop Protection Technical Services Free crop protection services from the Mapandan MAO. Farm inspection, plant analysis, and pest management recommendations. body: Civil Registry & Vital Records Name Correction (RA 9048) Correct your birth certificate under RA 9048. ₱3,000 for name change, ₱1,000 for clerical error. Description Republic Act No. 9048 authorizes the city or municipal civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries without the need for a judicial order. Requirements Proof of Publication (from PSA) Certificate of Live Birth (from PSA) NBI Clearance Police Clearance (from PNP) Certificate of Employment (if employed) / Affidavit of non-employment Marriage Certificate, Medical records, SSS records, land title, baptismal certificate Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and submit all required documents. File the petition for correction of clerical error. Pay the required fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the publication period to be completed. After publication and verification, claim the corrected birth certificate from the MCR. body: Health Services Nutrition & Immunization Program Free nutrition and immunization programs for children at the Mapandan RHU. Malnourishment intervention and NIP vaccines available. Description The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases. The nutrition program includes assessment, deworming, feeding with nutrient-dense food, and monthly monitoring. The immunization program administers age-appropriate vaccines after reviewing the child's records and checking vital signs. For immunization: BHW interviews child's information and reviews records. Midwife checks vital signs (weight and temperature). Midwife administers age-appropriate vaccine. Midwife advises parent on child care and expected outcome. Schedule next vaccination. body: Health Services Pre-Natal Consultation Free pre-natal consultation for antenatal women at the Mapandan Rural Health Unit. Lab tests and health teaching included. Description The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR), OB history, vital signs, Leopold's maneuver, fetal heartbeat assessment, and fundic height measurement. Routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg, RPR) are requested. The MHO conducts complete physical examination, interprets laboratory results, and provides health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. High-risk patients are referred to higher-level facilities. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Laboratory Results, Prescription for Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Procedure Register in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife encodes OB history, vital signs, and performs Leopold's maneuver. Request for routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg Screening, RPR test). MHO performs complete physical examination and interprets laboratory results. If high-risk, patient is referred to a higher level of facility. Health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 55 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation Family Planning

body: Health Services TB DOTS Treatment Free TB DOTS treatment at the Mapandan RHU. Sputum testing, GeneXpert, and anti-TB medication available. Description The RHU provides Directly Observed Treatment Short Course (TB DOTS) for patients with tuberculosis. The service includes registration, sputum examination, GeneXpert/TBDC testing, physical examination, and provision of anti-TB drugs with proper intake instructions. The MHO maintains patient confidentiality and monitors treatment compliance. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Prescription of Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Chest X-Ray PA Result (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Register in the log book. Midwife encodes data, vital signs, and asks about symptoms and duration. Submit sputum for examination. Sputum examination is conducted. Patient is referred to GeneXpert/TBDC for further testing. Consent is secured and confidentiality is maintained. MHO conducts physical examination of patient. Anti-TB drugs are given with record and patient is advised on proper intake. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Processing Time: 36 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Related Services Health Consultation Laboratory Examination

body: Youth Development Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) Register your youth organization with the LYDO in Mapandan under the YORP. Description The Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) administers the Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) as mandated by the SK Reform Act (RA 11769). Receive the Certificate of Registration upon approval (2 min). title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

title: Frequently Asked Questions — BetterMapandan.org
description: Common questions about government services, documents, and civic information for Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Support Frequently Asked Questions Answers to common questions about government services and civic information in Mapandan. General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .
